Fix failing accessible name tests

Some of our tests for accessible names have started failing after a Puppeteer update. We aren't totally sure why this is, but it appears that the nodes we're testing are now considered 'uninteresting' and are being pruned from the node list by Puppeteer.

This commit sets `interestingOnly: false` so that Puppeteer doesn't prune the node list prior to running the test.

https://pptr.dev/api/puppeteer.accessibility.snapshot#remarks

Expect errors from failing moduleResolution

We use Node for our typescript moduleResolution. This defaults to Node10, which means it doesn't support subpath exports.

html-validate happens to use subpath exports in v10.0.0, and this causes TypeScript to complain.

At some point, we probably should update our moduleResolution to nodenext , but doing that right now creates a lot of errors, so we're kicking the can down the road here and solving this by expecting the moduleResolution errors.

If this actually breaks our implementation, the tests themselves should fail, so the risk is small.

Add `aria-hidden` to Service Navigation toggle's initial HTML

`aria-controls` make VoiceOver keep the button visible in its rotor,
on desktop, and keep the button focusable on iPad.

Adding an `aria-hidden` ensures the button is correctly hidden without
introducing a breaking change. This is also the technique we'll use
in the component's JavaScript to hide the button fully as viewport gets resized.

Do not log express URL to console

The review app’s Express instance runs on port 8080, and then we run Browsersync on port 3000 which is the primary port we expect users to use when using the review app.

However at the minute we log the Express URL last in the terminal:

```
[app] [Browsersync] Access URLs:
[app]  ---------------------------------------
[app]        Local: http://localhost:3000
[app]     External: http://192.168.68.119:3000
[app]  ---------------------------------------
[app]           UI: http://localhost:3001
[app]  UI External: http://192.168.68.119:3001
[app]  ---------------------------------------
[app] [Browsersync] Watching files...
[app] Server started at http://localhost:8080
```

We’re showing the user 5 different URLs here, and putting the onus on them to work out which one they need to use.

Reduce the confusion by not logging the Express URL, and only outputting the BrowerSync URLs.

Bind express to localhost rather than all IPs

By default, `server.listen` will accept connections on 0.0.0.0 [1], which means you can access the review app using its local IP address from the same LAN (and, if there is a public IP, from the internet).

We have cases where we may want to allow users to connect to the review app externally (e.g. testing on a mobile device whilst connected to the same LAN as a developer machine) but we can use the BrowserSync URLs for this. There is no need to allow external connections from the express app itself.

Configure the Express app to bind to localhost instead, which only accepts connections from the same computer.

[1]: https://nodejs.org/api/net.html#serverlistenport-host-backlog-callback:~:text=If%20host%20is%20omitted%2C%20the%20server%20will%20accept%20connections%20on%20the%20unspecified%20IPv6%20address%20(%3A%3A)%20when%20IPv6%20is%20available%2C%20or%20the%20unspecified%20IPv4%20address%20(0.0.0.0)%20otherwise.

Only bind to localhost by default

By default, Browsersync will listen on all interfaces.

In line with security best-practises, default to only listening on localhost, which means by default we’d only accept connections from the same machine.

We have cases where we may want to allow users to connect to the review app externally (e.g. testing on a mobile device whilst connected to the same LAN as a developer machine), so preserve the existing behaviour if the environment variable `ALLOW_EXTERNAL_CONNECTIONS` is `”true”`.

Add a note to the ‘running locally’ doc to explain this.

Expect test server to run on localhost

It seems necessary to set this now that the express app is only listening for connections to localhost.

Handle new `unknown` type emited on `pageerror`

Puppeteer recently updated its `pageerror` event types
to no longer be just an `Error`, but also `unknown`. [1^]

This is because JavaScript code may `throw` not just `Error`
objects, but any kind of values. While Puppeteer handles some of the translation,
in some cases it can only forward the value from the browser,
which we then need to handle ourselves. [^2]

For now, we'll just output the value. If we end up seeing `[Array]` or similar
output, we can look at improving the output, but most errors we receive should be `Error` anyways.

[^1]: https://github.com/puppeteer/puppeteer/pull/14349
[^2]: https://github.com/puppeteer/puppeteer/blob/a2eb479ec506947e5912532dc414b37ec2bd7f5e/packages/puppeteer-core/src/cdp/utils.ts#L28

Make applied colour map private

This will avoid users accidentally remove applied colours by redefining `$govuk-applied-colours`
after importing `base`.

People can already define their own applied colours prior to importing GOV.UK Frontend.
If they need to define applied colours to one of GOV.UK Frontend's colour,
we could look at having that initial map accept not only a colour or string.
Add tests for existing features of `_govuk-frontend-properties.scss`

Remove change of link colour on hover for text and inverse variants

The very subtle change of colour was there to work around a Safari
issue where the change of thickness on hover wouldn't be enough to
trigger a redraw of the link. [1^]

Since then, we've also added a change of `text-decoration-skip-ink`
when the thinckness changes. [2^]

The changes of this property values are monitored by Webkit to trigger
a redraw. [3^].

This means the change of colour is no longer necessary (especially as
the bug is fixed since Safari 16.4 [4^] after a fix in Jan 2023 [5^]).

[1^]: https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/commit/683591e5980fcc706caf21a9c7fe9bfe46fe85cf
[2^]: https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/pull/2251
[3^]: https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/pull/8372/files#diff-dd44b7e08707f7ca39da2c55490b753d5d0b37c3a47a14738748e5fd023fc9daR1240-R1252

Merge pull request #6403 from alphagov/dependabot/npm_and_yarn/webpack-5.102.1

Disable BrowserSync UI by default

We rarely use it.

Disabling it saves a few resources and takes us down to only one URL listed in the BrowserSync ‘Access URLs’ in the console, reducing confusion for users.

Users can still enable it by setting the `ENABLE_BROWSERSYNC_UI` environment variable, and anyone that wants to use it on a regular basis can set the environment variable in their profile.

Swap innerHTML to textContent

innerHTML will return values that are HTML escaped (e.g. < becomes < and  & becomes &). textContent does not escape the values.

Although innerHTML will still work in this context, as the check only exists to reduce repetition and is not functionally necessary, textContent more accurately covers what is intended to be compared.

Co-Authored-By: Romaric Pascal <romaric.pascal@digital.cabinet-office.gov.uk>

Merge pull request #6587 from alphagov/footer-licence-removal-with-null--6.0

Move calls to `govuk-functional-colour` out of shorthand parameters

Having the function within shorthand params eg: `border` instead of `border-color` means that any problem with the `var()` call will break the entire attribute rather than just the colour attribute. This is therefore a means of damage control.

Test for usage of CSS variables for part of declaration values

Use an ad-hoc PostCSS plugin to check that CSS variables
are only used as part of a `box-shadow` declaration, and not
inside shorthand properties like `border` or `outline`.

CSS variables used for the whole value are OK, but if used
as part of a shorthand like `border` or `outline` and the custom property
is missing or invalid, the browser will also discard the other parts
of the shorthand (like the `border-width`), increasing the risk of broken
layout.

Make merged map of functional colours public

While users could set `$govuk-functional-colours` to override specific
functional colours, those were merged into a `$_govuk-functional-colours`
variable which was private when `@use`ing GOV.UK Frontend.

This was made to avoid users wiping the merged map if they redefined
`$govuk-functional-colours` after importing. Given Sass will ensure
GOV.UK Frontend keeps using the merged values, we're setting the map
public, which will let users `map.get` from it if necessary [^1].

[^1]: https://sass-lang.com/documentation/at-rules/import/#configuring-modules-through-imports

Allow `govuk-functional-colour` to resolve reference to colour palettes

Introduce a private (for now) helper, `_govuk-resolve-colour` to
resolve the colour from the palette corresponding to a `name`
and optional `variant` (defaulting to `primary`).

The helper is separate from `govuk-colour` so we can clearly distinguish
the two steps that go into resolving the colour:
 1. Validating the format of the reference (has a non empty name and if present a non-empty variant)
 2. Grabbing the colour from the palette given the resolved `name` and `variant`

This could allow to easily expand to resolving strings or lists into colours
from the palette without changing the behaviour of `govuk-colour`

Use `_govuk-resolve-colour` to output the custom properties

This will allow the `$govuk-functional-colours` map to store references

Use colour references in `$govuk-functional-colours`

This allows to resolve the colour at the time they're output,
rather than at the time the map is defined.

Add variable for the functional colour defaults

This helps document the available functional colours, as
before this the only available information in the Sass doc was:
`$govuk-functional-colours: ()` because the default were merged.

Making those defaults public allows the list to be present
in the Sass doc, as well as an opportunity to access back the defaults
if you overrode them. Note the absence of `!default` to prevent
the variable to be overriden before `import`.

To help users navigate the documentation a little better,
`$govuk-functional-colours` default has been updated to be
`$govuk-default-functional-colours`. While this makes the merge a little heavier
than an empty map, it lets users understand that the variable
is filled with the defaults unless they do anything to it.

Update default link colour to 10% shade of blue

When the service navigation component was created we used a 10% shade of blue for links to address concerns around the legibility of the links against the 95% blue tint background.

In #6659 we introduced the concept of a ‘surface-link’ to represent this use of colour, and also updated the cookie banner and footer to use the darker shade as we use the 95% tint background for those components.

We’ve since decided to simplify things by using the 10% shade for all links, not just those on 95% backgrounds.

We believe using the 10% shade also improves the legibility of links against white backgrounds.

This change also reduces the overhead on designers to understand when to use surface-link over link, especially as the change is so subtle.

Finally, it avoids an unfortunate interaction with the ‘no visited state’ mixin and modifier class, which re-sets the `:link` colour to the link functional colour.

With this change the contrast between links and white background increases from 5.16:1 to 6.07:1.

The contrast between links and the 95% tint background (#F4F8FB) increases from 4.84:1 to 5.69:1.

The contrast with text (#0B0C0C) is reduced from 3.78:1 to 3.22:1, but this still meets the minimum 3:1 ratio required to distinguish links from surrounding text on colour alone, for example when they do not have underlines (see WCAG 2.2 technique G183).

Move `optionalDependencies` to `devDependencies`

The separation causes issues for Dependabot which hoists some dependencies,
and leads to missing sub-dependencies in the `package-lock.json` (like `@octokit/core`),
which cause npm 11.8.0 not to be able to run `npm ci`.

Regrouping the `optionalDependencies` into `devDependencies` solves the issue with npm 11.8.0,
and shouldn't have any adverse effect as we don't use `--omit=optional` anywhere I could see.

as we require a strict 11.6.2 version but the installed version is 11.8.0:

The pinned version also did not match the minimum Node version as Node 24.11.0 installs with npm 11.6.1.

We do want to [skip 11.6.3](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/pull/6455)
which has issues with the `overrides` field of `package.json`

Avoid using `if` from settings

We generally try and avoid depending on things that exist in layers ‘above’ in the ITCSS pyramid. Using `if` from helpers breaks that rule.

As we’re resolving to a boolean anyway, we can just check if `list.index` returns null and negate the result to get the same result.

Don't add sourcemaps to package files

Our sass snapshots are generating a lot of extra lines and whitespace. This is because we're annotating both CSS and Sass files with sourcemapurl comments.

But annotating Sass files is useless: the sass compiler will just treat them as normal comments and generate the sourcemap from scratch. Things like PostCSS and CSSNano only ever see CSS files.

Furthermore, our sourcemaps in our package folder don't seem useful either - they're ostensibly mapping the dist files to their src equivalent, but this mapping is lost whencompiled - the browser will only ever use the compiled CSS, JS, etc - and they all map back to the dist folder.

Add `exports` field to shorten Sass URLs

When using Sass, resolve any string after `pkg:govuk-frontend` from `dist/govuk` rather than the root of the package. This allows to reduce the length of `pkg:` URLs.

The `./*` entry of `exports` has been moved to the bottom of the list as Node recommends ordering from more to least specific:

> Within the "exports" object, key order is significant. During condition matching, earlier entries have higher priority and take precedence over later entries. The general rule is that conditions should be from most specific to least specific in object order.
> - <https://nodejs.org/api/packages.html#self-referencing-a-package-using-its-name>

This allows users to still access files explicitely using `dist/govuk` should they wish to, making this a non-breaking change if they were doing: `@use "pkg:govuk-frontend/dist/govuk"`.

(In practice, it was also working with `./*` at the top of the list, I _think_ because no file matched `dist/govuk/dist/govuk` in the package so Node moved on to the next entry. But better safe than sorry.)

Ensure asset URL functions can be configure when importing `base`

Because of Sass modules, the `tools/font-url` and `tools/image-url` modules would not be able to get a reference to a Sass function in the global scope if `$govuk-font-url-function` and `$govuk-image-url-function` are set as strings.

To work around that we need code in the import-only file that turns the strings configured in `$govuk-font-url-function` and `$govuk-image-url-function` into Sass functions using `meta.get-function`.

However, `base` may be imported multiple times in a code base if a team structured their code like ours and `@import` base in each of their components so GOV.UK Frontend API is available. So we cannot go the "simple" route of doing `@forward "base" with (/* Asset URL function variables configured as functions */)`, which would make the second `@import` break compilation with `This module was already loaded, so it can't be configured using "with".`.

Instead we can:
- extract the actual forwarding of the `base` module in its own file, that we'll `@import` after configuring the asset URL function (unfortunately `@forward` and `@use` would have to come before any code can be run).
- have `settings/assets`'s import-url file become responsible for turning string-configured asset URL functions into Sass functions
- import `settings/assets` before the file forwarding the base module

Refactor configuration of asset URL function when importing `index`

Use the same structure as `base` for consistency

Maintain access to `base` members when importing a single component

Users can currently `@import` a single component files, which would not only output the component's CSS,
but also give access to GOV.UK Frontend's variables, functions and mixins from `base`.

Having each component `@forward "../../base"` maintains that functionality.

Make `index.scss` only `@forward` files

This will ensure the custom properties are always output first as we migrate layers.

As `@forward` statements need to come before any Sass code, the output of custom properties
would drift to the end of the CSS as we migrate each layer if we'd kept doing it with an explicit `@include` in `index.scss`.

Update custom properties index files

We want to get to a place where `govuk-exports` is only used in the context of `@import`.

For this to work, all partials that output CSS need to have:

- all CSS that it being outputted wrapped in a mixin, defined in a separate file
- an import-only file, which includes that mixin, wrapped in govuk-exports
- a normal partial file which includes the mixin

Index files also need to exist for both `@use` and `@import`:

- `_index.scss` which uses all of the partials
- `_index.import.scss` which imports all of the partials

With this approach we no longer need to wrap each layer in a mixin, or call that mixin from any other layer – using or importing the layer should result in the CSS being outputted only once – but we’ll only see the results of this once _all_ layers that output CSS have import-only files.

Show correct file size for files in PR stats

The `getFileSizeComparison` function accepts a set of `headFiles`, representing the files in the PR’s branch and a set of `baseFiles`, representing the files in the target/base branch.

We’re iterating over the `baseFiles` first, checking to see if that file exists in `headFiles` (if not, it’s been deleted) and if the size has changed (if not, we skip over it).

We then push the entry *from `baseFiles`* into the results with the percentage change.

This means that PRs currently show the size of the file as it is *in the target branch* instead of the size of the file in the PR’s branch.

Update the function to push the corresponding entry from `headFiles` into the results, so that we correctly show the size of the file in the PR branch.

This also means we need to change how we handle deleted files, because `headFile` will be `undefined` and so the returned object wouldn’t have a path or size. Refactor the function passed to map to return early with a valid `FileSizeWithPercentage` for deleted files to avoid this.

Update index to `@use` all layers

In #6972 we updated the core layer to use `@use`. Because of an issue with extending placeholders ‘shared’ between links and typography, we took a slightly different approach to the other layers, in that:

- `core/index` `used` the mixin files for all files in the layer and then included the mixins
- the individual files e.g. `core/lists` _also_ `used` the corresponding mixin file and called the mixin

The fact that we were still `importing` core from `index.scss` masked an issue with this approach.

When we update the index file to `use` each layer:

- `index` uses `core/index`, which includes all the mixins
- `index` uses, via `components/index`, `components/error-summary`
- `components/error-summary` uses `core/lists`, which includes the lists mixin a second time

@use prevents CSS being duplicated by only outputting the CSS for a given file once, but we now have two files both outputting the CSS for lists.

The tests are now failing – we’ll fix them in the next few commits.

Make core/index consistent with other layers

This means that each of the individual files are responsible for using and including their respective mixin.

With the mixin call only happening in one place, `@use` should take care of avoiding duplication of any CSS.

The tests are now failing for a different reason. The duplication of the lists CSS is no longer an issue, but we’re now seeing the issue with the contextual adjustments in core/typography not being extended by the concrete list classes in core/lists.

For example, the `.govuk-list + .govuk-heading-m` selector that we should get from extending `%govuk-list + %govuk-heading-m` is missing.

So, we’ll fix that issue in a future commit!

Stop using/importing lists from error summary

In the next commit we’re going to update `core/lists` to itself use `core/typography`.

That would mean that using or importing error summary would then give you the CSS for typography as well as for lists.

This is the only component that includes anything from core, despite other components relying on links, typography and lists.

Given this inconsistency, stop using/importing lists from error summary, and update snapshots for tests that were previously including the CSS for lists as part of the error summary.

A side-effect of importing core/lists was that the `error-summary/_index.import.scss` had access to base – with this import removed, we now need to import `base` so that we can use the `govuk-exports` mixin.

Technically some users may be relying on error-summary bringing in the styles for lists, and that this would be a breaking change. However, we think it’s highly unlikely that users would be using error summary without any of the other styles from core, and that on balance this should be a safe change to make.

Make core/lists use core/typography

This is what is required for the `.govuk-list` class in the lists mixin to correctly extend the placeholder classes in `core/typography`.

We need to do this from `_lists.css` rather than `_lists.mixin.scss` because using typography from the `_lists.mixin.scss` results in us *using* a file that outputs CSS when `lists.import.scss` is *imported* and this makes a big mess.

The CSS for typography moves to before lists in our CSS output. Update the snapshots for anything that includes core to reflect this.

For the sake of consistency [^1], make the same change to the import-only file for lists.

Update the Sassdoc for asset url functions

In #6767 we made it possible for `$govuk-image-url-function` and `$govuk-font-url-function` to be set to functions as well as strings.

In #6857 we then deprecated setting `$govuk-image-url-function` and `$govuk-font-url-function` to strings. Using a string does not work when loading GOV.UK Frontend as a module with `@use` or `@forward`, because each module can only see what it explicitly `@uses`.

Update the Sassdoc to reflect these changes, by:

- changing the type to Function | String | null [^1]
- updating the existing examples to set the variables to functions [^2]
- adding a new example where the variable is set to a string, but marking it as deprecated

I’ve also taken the opportunity to rewrite the Sassdoc description to make it clearer what the function should look like, and to add see annotations for the related parts of the API.

Closes #6945.

[^1]: I’ve also changed the default value of both settings from `false` to `null` as `null` is more appropriate and it means we can then include `null` in the types.
[^2]: There’s no longer an example using a function in the same file. This is because with `@use` the `@use` statement must come before any `@function` definitions (as flagged in https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/pull/6982#discussion_r3136995526)

Speed up branch filtering for preview branches

When creating a new branch to filter throw away the Git history
so that `git filter-branch` can run faster.

- use `--no-verify` to prevent linting on commits.
- use `npm ci` to ensure `build:package` command succeeds.
- checkout explicit branch to go back since there's no history anymore.

Drop sass-rails example from font/image function settings

These no longer seem relevant, given that:

- sass-rails hasn't seen an update for 7 years and does not support dart sass [1]
- dartsass-rails, which seems to be its replacement, seems to work alongside the Ruby assets pipeline rather than through the assets pipeline [2]
- image-url seems to be a feature of Sprockets (the old asset pipeline) which has now been replaced by Propshaft [3]
- propshaft’s migration steps [4] tell users to ‘replace all instances of asset helpers in your CSS files (e.g., image_url) with standard url() functions’, and that it will automatically convert these references to their fingerprinted equivalents [5]

(as flagged in https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/pull/6982#discussion_r3137918129)

[1]: https://github.com/rails/sass-rails/issues/445
[2]: https://github.com/rails/dartsass-rails#troubleshooting
[3]: https://guides.rubyonrails.org/asset_pipeline.html#sprockets-to-propshaft
[4]: https://guides.rubyonrails.org/asset_pipeline.html#migration-steps
[5]: https://guides.rubyonrails.org/asset_pipeline.html#fingerprinting-versioning-with-digest-based-urls:~:text=Finally%2C%20you%20can%20reference%20an%20image%20in%20your%20CSS%20like%3A

Fix hovering over the row of a small checkbox/radio button activating hover style

Currently, hovering anywhere over the row of a small checkbox will activate the hover style. This is misleading, as the input can only be checked by clicking on the visible input or the label and not anywhere on the row.

This commit rewrites the styles to instead depend on `:hover` on the input element. The styles still active when hovering either the input or the label because `<label>` elements relay their states to the inputs they're associated with: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics-other.html#selector-hover

> If preversion, version, or postversion are in the scripts property of the package.json, they will be executed as part of running npm version.
> The exact order of execution is as follows:
> 1. Check to make sure the git working directory is clean before we get started. Your scripts may add files to the commit in future steps. This step is skipped if the --force flag is set.
> 2. Run the preversion script. These scripts have access to the old version in package.json. A typical use would be running your full test suite before deploying. Any files you want added to the commit should be explicitly added using git add.
> 3. Bump version in package.json as requested (patch, minor, major, etc).
> 4. Run the version script. These scripts have access to the new version in package.json (so they can incorporate it into file headers in generated files for example). Again, scripts should explicitly add generated files to the commit using git add.
> 5. Commit and tag.
> 6. Run the postversion script. Use it to clean up the file system or automatically push the commit and/or tag.

Add logic to insert span element around HTML in start buttons

Start buttons use flexbox for layout and alignment. Part of how flexbox works includes it ignoring whitespace between adjacent flex children (elements and text nodes), causing them to render 'squashed' together.

For example, HTML in a start button like this:
Apply for <abbr>PIP</abbr> now

Would render like this:
Apply forPIPnow

By wrapping the entire HTML string in an element, we remove the elements and text nodes from being flex children, and whitespace renders as expected.

Change the colours displayed on this in-between page so they match the browsers
default colours (
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Values/system-color))

GOV.UK Frontend does not set `color-scheme` with a `dark` value
so these colours will not change to dark automatically, aligning with the existing behaviour.

This decision was made to ensure that there is no clear flash between
a light colour and dark colour which could arouse suspicion.

If GOV.UK Frontend supports dark mode in the future this overlay will then
support dark colours and a dark page will change to a dark overlay automatically.

Motivation behind this change is ensuring we dont use any hardcoded colours where possible
and rely on functional colours, in this case the appropriate colours are system level.

Update Service Navigation to use `inverse-text`

Once again, instead of relying on `link-style-inverse`, move to `link-style-text` and updates `--govuk-text-colour`. As the component does not have specific print styles we need to keep white for print as well (as the background will be blue.

Both the inverse and non inverse variants were updating `color` to allow for raw content to pick up the service navigation's colour. However, any application of a typography class would have overriden that so set the `--govuk-text-colour` as well.

Update Panel to use `inverse-text`

Use `inverse-text` colour in Notification Banner

Move the definition of the background next to the text colour adjustment to reduce risk of contrast issues. Because of how spacing is applied, this meant moving the code to the `__header` element rather than the `__title`.

To coordinate colours between the border and the title background, introduce a local `--_govuk-notification-banner-colour`. This allows to reduce the CSS needed to create the success variant and only change that variable.
To keep the text and background colour close to each other for maintenance, introduce a local `--_govuk-notification-banner-title-text-colour` set right next the `--_govuk-notification-banner-colour`.

Because of the leading `_` to mark these custom properties as private, we need to adapt the `custom-property-pattern` to allow a leading `_` before the kebab case pattern.

While the colour change through `govuk-link-style-inverse` would ensure the content is white,
it makes the change of colour far from wher the background is changed. Instead, relying on `govuk-link-style-text` for styling the link, we can group the change of background and text colour together. It'll also affect any content added to the header as an extra safety to ensure contrast against the background.

Because of the lack of functional colour for the generic header, the mixin has been extended to receive both a text and background colour. It defaults to palette colours for the generic header, until we settle on functions for those colours. The GOV.UK Header can then pass the functional `brand` and `inverse-text` colour it uses.

Make file input selector more specific

Now, instead of finding any input and failing if its type isn't "file",
it finds inputs with type "file" and fails if nothing is found.

Since version 7.0, when the multiple attribute is set on a file input,
Rails also renders a hidden input just before the file input, e.g.,

<input name="profile[profile_photo][]" type="hidden" value="">
<input id="profile-profile-photo-field" class="govuk-file-upload" multiple="multiple" type="file" name="profile[profile_photo][]">

This ensures that when the user submits a form with no files selected,
the form submission includes profile[profile_photo][], and Rails can
delete any files that are attached.

Remove silencing of mixed-decls warnings

Sass obsoleted this deprecation in 1.92.0.

Alter expected output of govuk-font mixin

Adjust Language navigation's top margin when in Service navigation
